critical_code_review_comments: FIXED — /app/backend/routes/mirror_v2.py::get_combined_pdf was building `by_instrument = {r['instrument']: r for r in results}`, which for closeness keys under 'MI-AS-36' (the stored result code). `_build_findings` then looked up `by_instrument.get('closeness')` and found nothing, so every closeness-dependent cross-check rule (6 of the 8 rules) was silently skipped in the combined PDF while POST /api/v2/mirrors/findings correctly returned them. This directly violated the spec 'findings match POST /api/v2/mirrors/findings for the same sessions' and could produce the 'No tensions worth reporting' line in the PDF while the same user's /mirrors screen showed real findings. Fix: reuse the already-built `best` dict (keyed by the session-side instrument string 'closeness') to call _build_findings. Verified end-to-end with a user whose closeness dimensions were forced to 7.0 anxiety and 7.0 avoidance — before the fix `Calm in general. Alarmed up close.` was returned by /mirrors/findings but missing from the combined PDF; after the fix it is present in both.

situation_notes.SITUATION_PDF_NOTES uses key 'MI-AS-36' for closeness — this remains correct because the combined endpoint builds `notes` by iterating results (which carry `instrument: 'MI-AS-36'`). Two different key conventions coexist in this file: session-side keys ('closeness', 'essential', 'personality', 'eq') and result-side codes ('MI-AS-36'). Worth a short comment in mirror_v2.py or a normalisation helper — this is exactly the kind of subtle mismatch that produced the bug above.

auth.py PATCH /me/situation accepts a raw dict — no pydantic model. Works fine, and matches the existing free-form claim endpoint; migrating to a `SituationRequest(BaseModel)` with `Literal[...]` would give the same 400 you already return for unknown values but with a structured error body. Not blocking.

DownloadCombined.js swallows the network error into a generic string — the console.error is present (`console.error('combined report download failed', err)`), matching the iteration-4 pattern applied to DownloadReport. Good.

The combined PDF does not include the Flag Check reflection anywhere — correct, since the review request calls it 'four ported psychometric instruments plus an unscored Flag Check' and the combined report is for the instruments only.

Combined endpoint's cursor is capped at 50 sessions (`to_list(50)`) — safe for any real user, but should be documented; per-instrument dedupe means only the four most-recent-per-instrument matter regardless.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Full 86-test suite lives across backend/tests/test_auth.py (16), test_iteration3.py (13), test_mirror_v2.py (15), test_pdf_report.py (26), test_iteration5.py (16). Run with `python -m pytest backend/tests -o addopts=''` (pytest.ini's xdist config is fine but slower on this container). Two things to remember about the combined PDF path: (1) the session's instrument string ('closeness') differs from the stored result's instrument code ('MI-AS-36'); INSTRUMENT_META, BODIES and SITUATION_PDF_NOTES all key by 'MI-AS-36' while _build_findings, sessions collection, and the /mirrors screen key by 'closeness'. Any code touching cross-instrument dicts needs to be careful which one it's using — the iteration-5 bug lived exactly here. (2) closeness answers are reversed based on item['key'] == 'R'; to force dimension values to 7.0 for testing findings, answer 7 for F items and 1 for R items (helper `_closeness_max_anxiety_answers()` in test_iteration5.py). PDF text extraction via pymupdf inserts \n at reportlab wrap points — always normalise with re.sub(r'\s+',' ', text) before substring assertions. Situation-switch signature phrases used for framing verification are pinned to short, unique fragments from situation_notes.py so tests are robust to copy edits elsewhere.
rca of the issue: Combined PDF cross-check section silently omitted every closeness-dependent finding. Reproduction: register a user, complete personality and closeness (with F=7, R=1 answers so closeness anxiety = 7.0), GET /api/v2/reports/combined.pdf and separately POST /api/v2/mirrors/findings with the same session_ids — the endpoint returned finding 'calm-general-alarmed-close' ('Calm in general. Alarmed up close.') but the PDF's cross-check section did not print it. Root cause: `get_combined_pdf` built `by_instrument = {r['instrument']: r for r in results}` where `r['instrument']` for closeness is the scoring-side code 'MI-AS-36' (set inside services/closeness_scoring.py:96), but _build_findings looks up `by_instrument.get('closeness')` — the session-side key used everywhere else in mirror_v2.py including /mirrors/findings. So `clo` was always None in the combined-PDF path and every rule that depended on anx/avo was skipped. Mitigation: pass the already-built `best` dict (keyed by session's instrument string) into _build_findings; this makes the two paths use the same key convention. Regression coverage added: test_combined_pdf_crosscheck_matches_findings_endpoint asserts that every finding title returned by /mirrors/findings appears verbatim in the combined PDF, and that the honest 'No tensions worth reporting' line only appears when the endpoint returns zero findings.
